rv.q: This superbly acted revival of Harold Pinter's 'Betrayal' is a master class in the art of theatrical subtlety.

Spall is, of course, much lesser known than his A-list co-stars, but it is Spall who runs off with the show at its crucial junctures, an imbalance that strikes me as perfect for "Betrayal," and, frankly, very much to the credit of these actors.
This impression is reinforced in this production, which looks great but is emotionally distant and a tad too tasteful.
A very tasteful, tranquil, and often beautiful performance of Betrayal begins.
By probing too many psychological motivations, Nichols makes these people understandable but awfully ordinary.
This Betrayal could use more of the same.
In the case of Betrayal, like Glengarry Glen Ross, the film is better than any stage production of it you're likely to see (I have seen several of each).
Likewise, finally, I can’t recommend this event to anyone who loves Pinter or Betrayal.

Although this production never catches its breath to reveal the slow-burning ashes of the past that the play usually makes vivid, knockout performances from both Craig and Weisz render it a Betrayal on fire.
